traits.notes: The seedling shows a whorled arrangement of simple, elliptic, entire-margined leaves at the apex, with a short petiole and shiny, glabrous leaf surface. The stem is green, herbaceous, and smooth. A pink tag is attached to one leaf, likely for identification purposes. Some minor damage is present on one leaf (small holes and a missing portion of the margin), but no other damage is evident. No reproductive structures are visible. All images show the same individual from slightly different angles, confirming the whorled leaf arrangement and consistent morphology.

=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (three or more leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images, forming a whorl at the top of the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, with no visible elongated internodes between leaf nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth and uninterrupted across all visible leaves)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are broadly elliptical, widest near the middle and tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is sharply pointed but not elongated)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is smoothly curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off perpendicularly from it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced relatively close together, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and form a distinct network, with multiple pairs per leaf)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaves have a glossy, reflective surface, likely due to waxy cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface; surface appears smooth)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, barely visible, and appear to be less than 1 cm in length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, no wings or grooves observed)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem is green, flexible, and lacks visible bark or woody texture, typical of young seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface is smooth, no visible hairs or trichomes)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is bright green, consistent across all images)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface is uniformly smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases; leaf attachment points show no appendages)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or milky fluid visible when stem or leaf is damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint or pulvinus visible at leaf base or petiole attachment)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed; leaves are not modified into tendrils)
F. Notes: The seedling shows a whorled arrangement of simple, elliptic, entire-margined leaves at the apex, with a short petiole and shiny, glabrous leaf surface. The stem is green, herbaceous, and smooth. A pink tag is attached to one leaf, likely for identification purposes. Some minor damage is present on one leaf (small holes and a missing portion of the margin), but no other damage is evident. No reproductive structures are visible. All images show the same individual from slightly different angles, confirming the whorled leaf arrangement and consistent morphology.
